A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WF-VAE and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. The duplicated supplementary material in v1 can be matched to the consolidated and extended supplement in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, computational-efficiency, video-generation, and ablation results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 4–7, plus supplementary wavelet analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds Inter4K reconstruction results and qualitative diffusion-pretraining and high-motion evaluations in the supplement.

M1.justification: The multilevel wavelet architecture, energy-flow pathway, Causal Cache procedure, and training objectives remain unchanged. The revised decoder symbols and channel-splitting wording clarify the feature extraction already described in v1.

E1.justification: v3 adds reconstruction evaluation on Inter4K videos at 480P and 720P in supplementary Section 5. Kinetics-400, WebVid-10M, Panda-70M, UCF101, and SkyTimelapse remain, making this a bounded extension of the existing video tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding main experiments. The new Inter4K evaluation uses existing comparators Allegro and CogVideoX. Newly discussed LiteVAE is not experimentally evaluated, and Open-Sora Plan serves as a downstream generation framework.

E3.justification: Supplementary Section 5 introduces 65-frame reconstruction tests at 480P/720P and Open-Sora Plan pretraining at 512×288. The retained experiments preserve their training schedules and evaluation settings. Relabeling reconstruction FVD as rFVD does not establish a metric change.

E4.justification: v3 adds an explicit reconstruction-robustness comparison across resolutions and additional high-motion qualitative comparisons with CogVideoX. Existing latent-channel, wavelet-loss, energy-path-width, architecture, and Causal Cache analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for performance comparisons. The supplementary energy/entropy boxplot reporting remains, and the new quantitative results use the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–5 retain their numerical values. New supplementary Table 3 reports Inter4K results: at 720P with 16 latent channels, WF-VAE-L has PSNR 34.82 and rFVD 19.27, versus CogVideoX's 34.24 and 24.82. These are newly reported settings, not improvements over v1 results. Qualitative examples are also added or replaced.

T1.justification: v3 removes the explicit conditions required for Causal Cache in v1 Equation 5, including chunk and kernel/stride constraints. The cache-size formula and supplementary derivation remain, as do the wavelet definitions and loss equations. This is a limited removal of formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about wavelet-driven energy flow, lossless Causal Cache, reconstruction quality, and computational efficiency. The abstract's 2× throughput and 4× lower memory claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2 adds an energy-based critique of LiteVAE's encoder–decoder asymmetry. Supplementary Section 5 explicitly interprets the new experiments as evidence of cross-resolution robustness and diffusion-pretraining applicability. Existing convergence explanations and the decoder-redundancy limitation remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly specifies that architecture ablations remove wavelet and inflow/outflow modules and set concatenation inputs to zero tensors. The supplement identifies Open-Sora Plan and its 512×288 pretraining resolution. Existing training hyperparameters and code/model access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds LiteVAE and a substantive contrast with its wavelet encoder, alongside LHNet, LHNetv2, and ConsisID citations. The broader positioning among video VAEs remains. Renumbering and publication-detail updates for retained references do not constitute additional research changes.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted prose and cross-reference corrections, updates affiliations, adds acknowledgments, and consolidates the duplicated supplement with an additional-experiments section. The main section sequence and most explanatory text remain closely aligned.

P2.justification: v3 adds the Inter4K table and supplementary pretraining/high-motion figure grids, replaces Figure 6 examples, clarifies Figure 2's decoder symbols, adjusts plot and highlight styling, and relocates Table 4. Duplicate supplementary displays are removed. These are localized changes within the retained document layout.

improvement.justification: v3 adds direct reconstruction-quality evidence at 480P/720P, extending v1's multi-resolution speed/memory evaluation, plus downstream pretraining examples. Clearer ablation details, LiteVAE positioning, and removal of duplicated supplementary material improve the paper's usefulness. The gains are limited by qualitative-only pretraining evidence and the unexplained removal of the cache-validity conditions.
